newsitem.title: USA: FedEx to get aircraft for hushkits.
newsitem.headline: FedEx to get aircraft for hushkits.

text.p: Federal Express Corp said on Monday that it will acquire 36 used DC-10-10 aircraft from UAL Corp's United Airlines in exchange for 59 727-200 heavyweight engine hushkits.
United will hold an option for 16 more hushkits, Federal Express said.

Also, Federal Express said it will introduce a new aircraft designation to its fleet, the MD-10. The aircraft is a modified version of the existing DC-10, designed in conjunction with McDonnell Douglas Corp and Honeywell Inc.
Federal Express is not putting a valuation on the hushkits it traded or the MD-10 program.
In a DC-10, the typical flight crew is three, but in the remodeled MD-10s the flight crew consist of two people, Federal Express spokesman Gregory Rossiter said.
Rossiter said the shipper will convert about 36 aircraft from its existing fleet to the MD-10.
The exchange of the aircraft and hushkits would commence in 1997 and continue over several years, the company said.
A McDonnell Douglas spokeswoman said the MD-10 has upgraded computers, navigation systems, compatability with Federal Express's MD-11 fleet and other advances over the DC-10-10.
Federal Express presently has a fleet of more than 560 aircraft with an additional 15 MD-11s, 19 A300-600s and 12 A310-200 aircraft scheduled for delivery in the next few years.
